hero.caption: This photo is from the boardwalk trail in Congaree National Park. Here, the trail goes through a forest of Bald Cypress trees, rising up to 120 feet above the swamp. These aren't the particularly large ones, but still a sight to see, especially with the "knees" coming out from the water for a root system that provides extra support.

images.filename: Bald Cypress Tress in Congaree National Park (52880948464).jpg
images.caption:
A forest of Bald Cypress trees stand in a "swamp" in Congaree National Park, South Carolina. While this area is similar to a swamp, and was even called one for a period of time, Congaree is considered "bottomland" with it's seasonal flooding and the largest tract of old growth bottomland in the United States.
These Bald Cypress trees are suited to life in these floodplains, with a root system that grows "knees" that stick up out of the water, potentially for support and stabilization in flooded lands. Several Cypress Knees are seen in the foreground.
This area was seen on a hike around the boardwalk of Congaree, taking a short detour onto Sims Trail.
